title: The Great Depression: the 1929 crash, mass unemployment and recovery
examples: How high did unemployment get in the Great Depression?
Why did the Depression spread around the world?

explain.say: On 24 October 1929, Black Thursday, panic selling hit the New York Stock Exchange; on 29 October prices collapsed again. Now look at the graph of real numbers. US unemployment was about 3 percent in 1929 and almost 25 percent by 1933, one worker in four. Britain's insured workers peaked at about 22 percent. Which line climbs faster?

draw.text: The Great Depression: the 1929 crash, mass unemployment and recovery

explain.say: A crash alone does not make a depression. Watch the chain. People lost savings, about 9,000 American banks failed between 1930 and 1933, firms cut output, and jobs vanished. US output fell by about a quarter. Then countries raised tariffs, taxes on imports, like America's Smoot-Hawley tariff of 1930. Which link turns a bad year into a bad decade?

stages.label: Loans recalled
stages.note: US money leaves Germany and Austria.

explain.say: Look at the map. American banks recalled loans from Europe. In May 1931 Austria's biggest bank, the Creditanstalt in Vienna, collapsed, and the crisis hit Germany, where about six million were registered unemployed by early 1932. Brazil's coffee and Japan's silk prices crashed too. Why would a bank failure in Vienna matter in Berlin?

Here is world trade shrinking, from the economist Charles Kindleberger's famous spiral. Monthly imports of 75 countries fell from about 3 billion gold dollars in January 1929 to under 1 billion in January 1933, about two thirds lost. Each country protected itself, and all grew poorer. Can you see the steps getting smaller?

draw.name: x-sizes
draw.unit: million gold $ of imports a month

explain.say: Why so deep? See the debate. Keynes said demand collapsed and governments should spend; Milton Friedman and Anna Schwartz blamed the US central bank for letting money shrink by a third. Barry Eichengreen showed that countries leaving the gold standard early, like Britain in 1931, recovered sooner. Great work. Challenge: compare Roosevelt's New Deal with Germany's response.

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Eichengreen: the gold standard spread it.

faq.a: The 1929 Wall Street Crash, waves of bank failures, falling spending, a shrinking money supply, tariffs that cut world trade and the gold standard, which spread the crisis between countries and stopped governments from easing money.
asks: What was the Wall Street Crash?

faq.q: How high did unemployment get in the Great Depression?
faq.a: In the United States it rose from about 3 percent in 1929 to about 25 percent in 1933. Among Britain's insured workers it peaked at about 22 percent in 1932, and Germany had about six million registered unemployed in early 1932.

faq.q: Why did the Depression spread around the world?
faq.a: American banks recalled loans from Europe, the gold standard linked countries' money, banks collapsed in Austria and Germany in 1931, tariffs cut trade, and prices for exports such as coffee, wheat and silk collapsed, hitting Latin America, Asia and Africa.
US President Franklin Roosevelt's programmes from 1933: bank reform, public works, farm support, job schemes and, in 1935, Social Security. Unemployment fell but stayed high until wartime spending.
A 1930 US law that raised taxes on thousands of imported goods. Other countries retaliated, and world trade shrank, deepening the Depression.
asks: How did tariffs make the Depression worse?

facts: US unemployment reached about 25 percent in 1933.
Austria's Creditanstalt bank collapsed in May 1931.
Britain left the gold standard in September 1931.

quiz.say: World imports fell from about 2,998 to about 992 million gold dollars a month. Roughly what fraction was left?
quiz.why: 992 divided by 2,998 is about 0.33, so about a third was left and two thirds lost.

wrong.1: Two thirds was the share lost, not the share left.
wrong.2: A tenth would be about 300 million.

quiz.say: According to Friedman and Schwartz, what made the Depression so severe?

options.show: The central bank letting money shrink
options.say: The central bank letting money shrink

quiz.why: They argued the Federal Reserve allowed bank failures and a one-third fall in the money supply.

wrong.1: Government spending was small at the start of the slump.
wrong.2: The New Deal came in 1933, after the worst collapse.
